tagline: One night a month, sit down and listen.
sector: Arts, culture and live music (monthly ticketed jazz and folk night)
founded_place_size: Founded 2021 in the back room of a bar, Providence, Rhode Island. Tiny: two organisers, ninety seats, one night a month.
about: Velvet Hour is a monthly ticketed jazz and folk night held in the ninety seat back room of a Providence bar. Two sets, no support, one camera in the same corner every month. The night sells intimacy and musicianship to people who read a lineup carefully, so everything we make should feel like a good room rather than a club or a concert hall.
audience: Lineup literate adults roughly thirty to sixty who pay eighteen to twenty five dollars to sit close and listen. Locals who follow the acts, not a party crowd.
price_positioning: Mid, intimate. An eighteen to twenty five dollar ticket. Never budget club, never black tie concert hall.

palette.name: Lamp Cream
palette.usage: Every act name, the venue name, billing, door time, price and body type set on Back Room Green or over footage, as on velvet_hour_listing_card_printer.pdf; the one ink of the moth and lamp mark, as painted on velvet_hour_lampbox.jpg; and the ground of a small-print strip, as the footer strip of velvet_hour_listing_card_printer.pdf.

palette.usage: The main ground: the poster ground, the film end card and any solid panel, as the card ground of velvet_hour_listing_card_printer.pdf and the board the mark is painted on in velvet_hour_lampbox.jpg. Not a type colour.

palette.usage: Small print and all type on a Lamp Cream ground, as the footer paragraph of velvet_hour_listing_card_printer.pdf, and the plain well behind a photograph, as its photo well. Never type on Back Room Green.

palette.usage: Hairline rules and the date line, as the rule above the act name and the date on velvet_hour_listing_card_printer.pdf. Always flat. Never a ground, a panel or an act name.

palette.name: Dust Rose
palette.usage: The tagline “One night a month, sit down and listen.” only, set small, as the kicker line on velvet_hour_listing_card_printer.pdf. Never a ground, a panel or an act name.

typography: Velvet Hour runs a four step scale. Step 01, display, is Adobe Caslon Pro Regular 400 at 96 pt on 104 pt leading, tracking minus 5 units on the given name and 120 units on the true small caps surname: the headline act stacked on two lines, given name above surname, so the second line falls quieter than the first. Step 02, subheading, is the same face and stack at 48 pt on 54 pt for support acts, tracking minus 3 units on the given name and 120 units on the small caps surname, with the date line beneath at 24 pt on 30 pt in National 2 Regular. Step 03, body, is National 2 Regular at 11 pt on 16 pt, tracking 0, to a maximum of 65 characters, with the ticket line in National 2 Medium at the same size. Step 04, fine print, is National 2 Regular at 8 pt on 12 pt with tracking of plus 25 units. The film title card carries the same two line stack at 54 px on 64 px. An act name is never set in the sans.
voice: Plain, affectionate, low key. Talks about the room and the players, never hypes. Short sentences, no exclamation, lets the act's face and the music do the work.
brand_assets_status: Our mark, a moth over a lamp inside a hairline arc of small caps type, was made by the designer who set up the night, and the source file went with them when they left. All that survives is the mark painted in one cream ink on the dark green lamp box by the door, which is why it has to be rebuilt from that as real artwork. No brand typeface was ever formally chosen, so the type system is open for you to set.
values: Story first, no gimmicks. Clean, coherent, honest to the room. We would rather look like a place people sit and listen than like a night that is trying too hard.

type_system.signature_move: Every act name stacks on two lines, given name above surname, the surname in true Adobe Caslon Pro small caps tracked 120 units so the second line falls quieter than the first. The stack holds at 96 pt for the headliner, 48 pt for supports and 54 px on the film title card.
rules: Never set an act name in the sans.
Every act name stacks on two lines, given name above surname.
The surname is always true Caslon small caps tracked 120 units. Never fake small caps by scaling capitals.
National 2 Regular sets billing and dates, Medium sets the ticket line.
No exclamation marks and no hype. Short sentences, and the act's face and the music do the work.

palette_rules.distribution: Back Room Green is the main ground for the poster, the film end card and any solid panel, as on velvet_hour_listing_card_printer.pdf. Lamp Cream is a ground only for a small-print strip, where all type is Warm Ink, as that card's footer. On Back Room Green and over footage, act names, the venue name, billing, door time, price and body are Lamp Cream; the date line may be Ember Amber and the tagline Dust Rose, as on the card. The mark is drawn in flat Lamp Cream on Back Room Green, as painted on velvet_hour_lampbox.jpg. Ember Amber and Dust Rose are accents for hairline rules, the date line and the tagline only, together no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area, never a ground, a panel or an act name.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow, glow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, any type or the mark, and no scrim, vignette, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over footage or a photograph: type sits straight on the footage or on a solid Back Room Green card or panel. In the films a card or line may cut or fade in and out as a whole; colour and opacity are judged on a settled frame.
palette_rules.forbidden: No gold, foil, metallic sheen, glow, drop shadow or other display gimmick on any type, rule, panel or the mark, as the brand's own typography note rules out (“No display gimmicks, no gold foil gestures.”); Ember Amber is always a flat colour. No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, grounds, panels, rules or the mark.
palette_rules.photography: Footage and photographs keep their own colour and are never tinted, duotoned or washed toward the palette. The six takes keep the warm lamp light and the green room as filmed. The act photographs keep natural skin: next_month_act_01.jpg is not pushed grey or orange, and the printed halftone dots in next_month_act_04.jpg are not resampled into a moire. A bar still such as velvet_hour_still_07.jpg keeps natural skin under its warm cast, not taken grey by a whole-frame neutral balance.
